papers.title_en: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
papers.authors: Kleanthis Avramidis, Ivan Tashev, Dimitra Emmanouilidou
papers.evidence: 轻量级脑电图基础模型，学习离散神经编码和可迁移特征用于解码
papers.tldr: 针对现有脑电图基础模型因规模过大难以部署在资源受限设备的问题，本文提出轻量模型BrainCodes，采用量化神经分词器与时空编码器，在超过800小时、1000余名参与者的数据上自监督预训练，通过通道位置编码和辅助目标捕获空间连接及窄带振荡特征。该模型在睡眠分期、注意力评估和认知负荷估计等任务上达到或超越现有最优，同时可训练参数减少最高97%，并能有效迁移至低资源可穿戴设备，还提供了表征几何与不变性的评估框架。
papers.abstract_en: Recent electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models increasingly emphasize model scale, potentially limiting their deployment on resource-constrained devices and in everyday environments. We argue that transferable EEG features can instead be learned with a compact architecture and introduce BrainCodes, a lightweight foundation model pretrained through self-supervised learning on more than 800 hours of recordings from over 1,000 participants. Our architecture combines a quantization-based neural tokenizer with a spatiotemporal encoder that supports arbitrary electrode configurations. The pretraining objective explicitly encourages representations that capture spatial connectivity through channel positional encoding, and sensitivity to narrowband neural oscillations through an auxiliary training objective. Our model matches or surpasses the state of the art across diverse neurophysiological monitoring tasks, including sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation. BrainCodes transfers effectively to low-resource wearable devices while using up to 97% fewer trainable parameters than comparable architectures. Beyond predictive accuracy, our evaluation framework characterizes the geometry and invariances of learned EEG representations across measurable spatial, temporal, and spectral signal properties.

papers.title_en: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
papers.authors: Julian Silva, Jaliya Kodithuwakku, Navindu Sirimanna, Shaveen Herath, Wageesha N. Manamperi, Joshua P. Kulasingham
papers.evidence: 基于EEG的听觉注意解码用于目标说话人提取
papers.tldr: 针对多说话人场景下目标说话人提取的低保真与窄带限制，提出 NeuroCodec，首个在神经音频编解码器潜在空间中运行的生成式 EEG 引导 TSE 框架。该方法通过图卷积建模 EEG 空间依赖，利用注意力与 Mamba 融合跨模态表示，并采用六阶段训练课程实现高保真生成。实验显示其在感知指标上超越基线，支持 44.1kHz 宽带重建，并扩展为因果流式以适配助听设备。
papers.abstract_en: Driven by recent advancements in hearing assistive devices, target speaker extraction (TSE) in multi-talker environments has drawn significant attention. To address this, hearing technologies identify attention using neural signals recorded via electroencephalography (EEG) to guide TSE, enabling neuro-steered auditory attention decoding. However, most existing techniques rely on time-frequency masking, which suffers from low fidelity in spectro-temporally overlapping regions and is often restricted to narrowband audio. In contrast, we introduce NeuroCodec, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first generative EEG-guided TSE framework operating in the latent space of a neural audio codec. Specifically, NeuroCodec models spatial EEG dependencies via graph convolutions and fuses cross-modal EEG and speech representations through attention mechanisms and Mamba-based temporal modeling. We further introduce a six-phase training curriculum that progressively incorporates latent reconstruction, multi-scale spectral, and adversarial objectives to ensure stable, high-fidelity speech generation. Experiments on the public Cocktail Party and KUL datasets show NeuroCodec outperforms baselines, across several perceptual metrics. A listening experiment with 20 participants validated that NeuroCodec offers greater perceptual accuracy, achieving a mean score of 82.24 compared with 49.63 for M3ANet. Additionally, the proposed method is seen to enable 44.1 kHz reconstruction with spectral content extending up to 20 kHz, further supporting the perceptual results. Finally, we extend NeuroCodec with a causal streaming formulation suited for real-time processing, providing a basis for hearing assistive devices.

papers.title_en: Probing Spatial and Spectral Grounding in EEG Foundation Models
papers.authors: Kleanthis Avramidis, Ivan Tashev, Dimitra Emmanouilidou
papers.evidence: 探测方法揭示 EEG 基础模型如何利用空间/频谱特征
papers.tldr: EEG基础模型评估通常只看下游准确率，无法判断模型是否利用生理可解释的信号结构。本文提出空间和频谱基础探针，在五个已发布模型上测试，发现表征敏感性与下游依赖存在解离：电极身份可被编码但不影响分类，频谱细节可区分但多数模型对模拟临床标记无特定反应。这表明基础探针能补充性能评估，揭示模型真正编码和依赖的内容。
papers.abstract_en: EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure. We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. We apply these probes to five published EEG foundation models across motor-imagery and seizure recordings. Our experiments reveal differences in both representational sensitivity and downstream reliance. Electrode identity may be encoded without influencing downstream classification: permuting LaBraM's positional codes heavily displaced its embeddings yet reduced motor-imagery accuracy by only 1.2 points, while spectral details may be discriminable without producing specific responses to simulated clinical markers, as only REVE exceeded a spectral baseline on this task. These dissociations are hidden in common benchmarks, demonstrating how grounding probes can complement performance-based evaluation by revealing what EEG foundation models encode and what their predictions depend on.

papers.title_en: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
papers.evidence: CCA用于从多模态神经影像数据恢复共同成分，是联系外部变量与神经活动的数学框架。
papers.tldr: 本文整合统计学CCA、信息论公共信息与工程子空间方法，解决从多观测中无监督恢复公共成分的跨领域问题。从信息论基础到线性、非线性CCA，涵盖核、深度、概率形式及可辨识条件，揭示方法间等价性与类比，提供自包含教程。
papers.abstract_en: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to Gács and Körner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.

papers.title_en: A Bayesian Distance-Weighted Ising Model for Task-Related Regional Analysis of Neuroimaging Data
papers.authors: Heesang Lee, Jongrak Park, Seoyoung Choi, Bokgyeong Kang, Nial Friel, Sanghoon Han, Jaewoo Park
papers.evidence: 贝叶斯 Ising 模型关联任务标签与功能神经影像信号
papers.tldr: 本文针对神经影像分析中认知状态分类、任务相关脑区识别和功能连接分析通常分离的问题，提出贝叶斯距离加权 Ising 模型，统一整合分类、区域重要性与连接分析。该方法采用基展开和辅助变量 MCMC 处理不等时间网格与难解归一化常数。在 fNIRS 数据上实现高分类精度，并揭示年龄相关的区域贡献和连接模式差异。
papers.abstract_en: Neuroimaging analysis commonly involves classifying cognitive conditions, identifying task-relevant brain regions, and examining functional connectivity. These objectives are typically addressed separately, without a model-based framework. In contrast, we propose a Bayesian distance-weighted Ising model that integrates classification, regional importance, and connectivity analysis. The model captures dependence among task labels based on connectivities between functional signals, while region-of-interest (ROI)-specific interaction parameters account for spatial heterogeneity and quantify regional contributions to task discrimination. However, inference is challenging because the signals may be observed on unequal time grids and the likelihood function contains an intractable normalising constant. To address this, we use a basis expansion and an auxiliary variable Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm. We apply the method to functional near-infrared spectroscopy data from younger and older adults, comparing resting-state and task-related activity. The model achieves high classification accuracy and reveals age-dependent patterns of regional importance and connectivity. Among younger adults, the left orbitofrontal cortex contributes more strongly to task discrimination than the dorsolateral prefrontal and frontopolar cortices, whereas regional differences are less evident among older adults. Older adults also exhibit greater bilateral connectivity between corresponding ROIs, consistent with reduced hemispheric lateralisation.
